steps.text: Early 1094
The nomadic city of Kazdel, Kazdel

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Please wait, General!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You are too impatient.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: But General! The Duke's envoy was almost ready to spit on—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Did we get what we wanted?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We got partial usage rights for the industrial area and the right to cross the border... but did it have to be so humiliating?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The Victorian dukes have you at their beck and call, treating us Sarkaz like tamed beasts. This is not what our soldiers redeployed from the civil war were promised, General!

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Is this not all that we desired?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Perhaps you would prefer the Victorians treat the Sarkaz as their greatest enemy from the beginning, banding together to face us?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I understand. I know it's necessary for our enemies to think us weak, but this...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Many within our ranks feel this is terribly dishonorable—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Did I promise them honor?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Do the Sarkaz have honor in the eyes of the Victorians?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You have been far too impetuous lately, Manfred.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Dignity is of high import.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You fight for the rights of your men, and thus do people respect you. Were these ordinary times, perhaps I too would commend you.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But do you remember what we are here to do? We are preparing to steal the heart of a nation.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: To bring the greatest empire on this great land to its knees.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Their prejudices have left them weak, and the Sarkaz are in hunger.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: What we truly need is neither honor nor respect.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...I understand.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Are our men prepared?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Ready to depart at a moment's notice. Our people sent in advance to Londinium will support us.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The final deadline for our arrival as dictated by the Duke of Cavendish's request is fast approaching. We can set out at any time.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Good.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Then we march to destroy Victoria.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have you been on duty this entire time?

steps.name: Military Commission Guard
steps.text: Yes, sir.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Stand down for now. I wish to be alone for a while.

steps.name: Military Commission Guard
steps.text: Of course, sir.
Once the guards leave, Manfred takes out a wine glass he had placed to the side.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Care for a drink?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You never drank before.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I still don't.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: But the General has ordered me to learn Victorian 'etiquette', all preparation for our upcoming duty.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I have learnt rather recently that those nobles pair every meal with multiple kinds of wine, each requiring its own unique glass.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Remember when we were young and the General led us to an ancient battlefield for swordplay? The night was cold, and only after the General made some soup did we realize we had nothing to hold it in.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Thankfully, the battlefield was nothing short of spent shells, and you used those to fashion four cups.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You, me, the General, and Her Highness, carrying cups made out of shell casings while sitting in front of the fire.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I remember. It was a peaceful night.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Just like this one.
The frigid moonlight of late winter falls through the window. Manfred rests his hand upon his sword hilt that was equally as cold.
The air is still, and the two of them can hear the other's heartbeat.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You're going to Londinium tomorrow.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I know you wished to see the General.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And you couldn't. Otherwise, you wouldn't have come to see me.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I gave up.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I found that when I caught a glimpse of him from a distance, the first thought that came to my mind was that I should kill him, there and then.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Then you should applaud yourself for maintaining some reason.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And so you decided to come to me?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I heard you've improved your swordsmanship. Why don't we see for ourselves?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I've never been able to best you.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Don't beg for mercy before you've even fallen.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There was the one time we fought in Her Highness's study.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We knocked down an entire bookshelf, and the General took our weapons away and made us tidy up the room within thirty minutes.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I knew that you did it on purpose, wanting attention from Their Highnesses.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Is that so?
Ascalon hides herself away into the shadows in the blink of an eye.
Another blink, and Manfred feels a chill running across the side of his neck.
He didn't have the time to draw his sword and fight back. He didn't have the time to even think about fighting back.
Perhaps he was too tired?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: If I cut your neck here, at least there will be no need for you to die in Londinium. I can just throw your corpse into the furnace.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: It would spare many from dying on a distant battlefield in a foreign land.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If you've made your decision, then kill me here. It will be your final chance.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You've made yours, I see.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The General says you lack conviction, but I don't think he is entirely correct.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You shouldn't speak so much when someone has your life in her hands.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: It is only recently that I've realized I'm not as resolute as you.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We have been brought to where we are by the invisible tides of fate, but ever since the day this war started... There is no going back for us.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Then do your best to survive.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I won't hold back next time.
The silent assassin stows her blade up her sleeve, then slowly steps back into the shadows.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...Neither will I.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: If only this was our last meeting.
Rhodes Island of Babel, Kazdel
A cold wind scatters the thick clouds of late winter, allowing sunlight to peek through the gaps and spread out across the bridge of the ship.
Down the stairs, Ascalon stands unmoving by a guardrail.
She shuts her eyes tight, enjoying the fleeting warmth of the sunshine.
Above the stairs, there is a clear rustling of cloth dragging against the ground.
A shadow flit across the assassin's face, blocking out the rays of sunlight.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Sorry Ascalon, did I disturb your rest?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I thought I wouldn't make any sound, if I took off my shoes.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No. You are welcome at any time.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The ground's cold. You should put your shoes back on, Your Highness.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Nothing you wish to tell me, Ascalon?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The reason you returned to Kazdel.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...It was my own decision.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I thought you wouldn't agree, and I didn't know how to bring it up with Your Highness...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why would I not agree, Ascalon? Since it was your decision, I would trust your judgement.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Did you manage to see them?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: ...Manfred and Theresis are both well.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I can believe that. They're strong men.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We should finish our preparations soon as well. The operation to retake Kazdel isn't too far off now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Why does your brow seem even more furrowed than before?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Our recent combat plans have been radical, and they've won us some battles too.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Still, I've been feeling uneasy.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Babel has changed a lot, especially...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The Doctor.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The Doctor has changed a lot too... become more efficient, more clinical. It's like... the Doctor's now a machine that never makes mistakes.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That's just what a commander should be, no? Why would that make you worry?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: We've got an incredible commander now, sure... But I think I trust the weirdo who kept falling off a burdenbeast more.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Is now really the best time to attack Kazdel, Your Highness?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Your intuition has always been on the mark.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: You've had your worries too?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Do you remember?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We've faced countless insurmountable odds over the years, but we've overcome them all.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I believe that we can go through what comes next as well.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: We've always been in danger, yes...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Babel carries the hopes of many, Ascalon. Faith has gotten us this far, and we cannot stop now.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: We have always been at a disadvantage against the Military Commission. Now, most of their forces have redeployed to Londinium. It is a one-of-a-kind opportunity. We have no choice.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I will be at your side, keeping you safe.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: No, Ascalon.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: In the future, you must go further afield, to protect others.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Relax for now, and bask in the sunlight for a moment.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Your Highness...

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh, right, remember to not always rest on your feet. If you're tired, you should go and enjoy a nice nap in your room.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: I'll remember.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Hm...
The sunlight shines upon Ascalon's face once more.
It is bright and warm. But the moment the shadow faded away, she suddenly felt some peculiar emotion flooding through her chest.
At the time, she was unable to describe what it was. It dawned on her many years later, on another sunny day.
It was an unwillingness to part ways.
Londinium, Victoria

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Mercenaries!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Message from His Grace the Duke: Storming Londinium like this was well done.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Assemble in Central in an hour. You'll be reviewed there, then you'll receive your bounty.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hey! Did you get all that?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Yes. Your orders have been received.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Do let the Duke know on my behalf that we will be there on time.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Sarkaz thank him for his generosity.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: Uppity devils...
It could well be a rare fine day in Londinium, if it were not for the gun smoke filling the air. From atop the towering city walls, one can see the entire lay of this ancient city.
The General in his bloodstained uniform says not a word, his gaze fixed on the great edifice in the center of the city.
In the skies above Londinium, a dark cloud floats by.
